source.title: Dynamic modulation of decision biases by brainstem arousal systems

confidence_rationale: Trial-by-trial human evidence that phasic (pupil-linked) arousal reduces the influence of a pre-existing bias on choice, with fMRI showing the bias reduction is predicted by phasic brainstem responses including LC. The follow-up (de Gee et al. 2020, eLife 9:e54014, PMID 32543372) generalises this to both liberal and conservative biases, to mice, and to memory-based decisions, and localises it to evidence-accumulation bias. That is the behavioural signature MECH-084 predicts (phasic NA weakens the prior's hold relative to current evidence). Capped because the evidence is correlational, pupil is not NA-specific (several brainstem nuclei covary), and 'decision bias' is a prior on choice rather than a top-down constraint on sampling.
failure_signatures: The bias reduction is predicted by phasic responses of several neuromodulatory brainstem centres, not LC alone, and pupil also tracks cholinergic activity (see Reimer et al. 2016 in this pull) -- the effect is not attributable specifically to NA.

The design is correlational (spontaneous trial-to-trial pupil variation); no NA manipulation establishes that NA causes the bias reduction or that a matched-arousal, non-NA control would fail to reproduce it.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Large task-evoked pupil responses (a proxy of phasic arousal) predict a reduction in decision bias across sensory modalities and task protocols; the pupil-linked bias reduction is accompanied by modulation of choice-encoding pattern signals in parietal and prefrontal cortex and is predicted by phasic, pupil-linked responses of several brainstem neuromodulatory centres including the noradrenergic LC. Phasic arousal suppresses decision bias trial by trial.
mapping.ree_translation: If a standing bias is read as the E2-side prior pressing on how current evidence is weighed, then phasic arousal loosening that bias on the trials where it fires is the behavioural form of MECH-084's 'high NA reduces E2's constraining influence on E1'. The trial-by-trial (phasic) timescale matches the claim's phasic 'snap' rather than a tonic state effect.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Decision/choice bias is a prior on the response, not a prior on where to sample; the paradigm has no unexpected cue or reorientation. Pupil-linked arousal is multi-transmitter, so the NA attribution is correlational and partial.
mapping.source_context: Healthy human adults; visual and auditory detection/discrimination tasks with pupillometry; fMRI including brainstem nuclei (LC, VTA, SN, basal forebrain, superior colliculus).

confidence_components.notes: eLife, multiple datasets, replicated and extended across species in de Gee 2020. Mapping moderate: right direction and timescale, wrong DV (choice bias, not sampling allocation) and not NA-specific.
